0 # lazygit

A simple terminal UI for git commands. ## Description Lazygit is a terminal UI for git commands that makes working with git easier and more intuitive. Instead of typing complex git commands, you can use a simple visual interface to perform common git operations. ## Features ### Stage individual lines Press space on the selected line to stage it, or press `v` to start selecting a range of lines. You can also press `a` to select the entirety of the current hunk. ### Interactive Rebase Press `i` to start an interactive rebase. Then squash (`s`), fixup (`f`), drop (`d`), edit (`e`), move up (`ctrl+k`) or move down (`ctrl+j`) any of TODO commits, before continuing the rebase by bringing up the rebase options menu with `m` and then selecting `continue`. ### Cherry-pick Press `shift+c` on a commit to copy it and press `shift+v` to paste (cherry-pick) it. ### Bisect Press `b` in the commits view to mark a commit as good/bad in order to begin a git bisect. ### Nuke the working tree For when you really want to just get rid of anything that shows up when you run `git status`, press `shift+d` to bring up the reset options menu and then select the 'nuke' option. ### Amend an old commit Pressing `shift+a` on any commit will amend that commit with the currently staged changes (running an interactive rebase in the background). ### Filter You can filter a view with `/`. For example, filter down the branches view and then hit `enter` to view its commits. ### Worktrees You can create worktrees to have multiple branches going at once without the need for stashing or creating WIP commits when switching between them. Press `w` in the branches view to create a worktree from the selected branch and switch to it. ### Undo Lazygit provides powerful undo capabilities. See the documentation for details. ### Commit graph Lazygit displays a visual commit graph showing the relationship between commits. ## Installation Lazygit is available through various package managers: ### Binary Releases Download pre-built binaries from the releases page. ### Homebrew (macOS and Linux) ```sh brew install lazygit ``` ### MacPorts (macOS) ```sh sudo port install lazygit ``` ### Scoop (Windows) ```sh scoop install lazygit ``` ### Chocolatey (Windows) ```sh choco install lazygit ``` ### Winget (Windows) ```sh winget install -e --id=JesseDuffield.lazygit ``` ### Arch Linux ```sh sudo pacman -S lazygit ``` ### Fedora / CentOS Stream ```sh sudo dnf install lazygit ``` ### Debian and Ubuntu ```sh sudo apt install lazygit ``` ### NixOS ```sh nix-env -iA nixpkgs.lazygit ``` ### FreeBSD ```sh pkg install lazygit ``` ### Conda ```sh conda install -c conda-forge lazygit ``` And many other package managers. Check your system's package manager for availability. ## Usage Call `lazygit` in your terminal inside a git repository: ```sh $ lazygit ``` You can also add an alias for convenience: ```sh echo "alias lg='lazygit'" >> ~/.zshrc ``` ### Changing Directory On Exit If you change repos in lazygit and want your shell to change directory into that repo on exiting lazygit, add this to your `~/.zshrc` (or other rc file): ```sh lg() { export LAZYGIT_NEW_DIR_FILE=~/.lazygit/newdir lazygit "$@" if [ -f $LAZYGIT_NEW_DIR_FILE ]; then cd "$(cat $LAZYGIT_NEW_DIR_FILE)" rm -f $LAZYGIT_NEW_DIR_FILE > /dev/null fi } ``` Then `source ~/.zshrc` and from now on when you call `lg` and exit you'll switch directories to whatever you were in inside lazygit. To override this behaviour you can exit using `shift+Q` rather than just `q`. ## Configuration ### Config File Location Default path for the config file: - Linux: `~/.config/lazygit/config.yml` - MacOS: `~/Library/Application Support/lazygit/config.yml` - Windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\lazygit\config.yml` You can create repo-specific config files in `/.git/lazygit.yml`. Settings in these files override settings in the global config file. ### Keybindings Lazygit provides extensive keyboard shortcuts for all operations. See the keybindings documentation for a complete list. ### Custom Commands Lazygit has a flexible custom command system that allows you to extend its functionality with your own commands. ## Documentation For more detailed documentation, see the `docs/` directory, which includes: - Configuration guide (Config.md) - Custom command keybindings (Custom_Command_Keybindings.md) - Custom pagers (Custom_Pagers.md) - Undo/Redo functionality (Undoing.md) - And more ## FAQ ### What do the commit colors represent? - Green: The local commit is not yet on the remote - Yellow: The commit is on both local and remote - Red: The local commit is not on the remote but the remote has commits that the local doesn't ## License See LICENSE file for details. ---- Config.md Custom_Command_Keybindings.md Custom_Pagers.md Fixup_Commits.md README.md Range_Select.md Searching.md Stacked_Branches.md Undoing.md keybindings

See the keybindings documentation for a complete list. ### Custom Commands Lazygit has a flexible custom command system that allows you to extend its functionality with your own commands. ## Documentation For more detailed documentation, see the `docs/` directory, which includes: - Configuration guide (Config.md) - Custom command keybindings (Custom_Command_Keybindings.md) - Custom pagers (Custom_Pagers.md) - Undo/Redo functionality (Undoing.md) - And more ## FAQ ### What do the commit colors represent? - Green: The local commit is not yet on the remote - Yellow: The commit is on both local and remote - Red: The local commit is not on the remote but the remote has commits that the local doesn't ## License See LICENSE file for details. ---- Config.md Custom_Command_Keybindings.md Custom_Pagers.md Fixup_Commits.md README.md Range_Select.md Searching.md Stacked_Branches.md Undoing.md keybindings

python3 <<'EOF'
text = """    -h --help               Displays help with available flag, subcommand, and positional value parameters.
    -p --path               Path of git repo. (equivalent to --work-tree=<path> --git-dir=<path>/.git/)
    -f --filter             Path to filter on in `git log -- <path>`. When in filter mode, the commits, reflog, and stash are filtered based on the given path, and some operations are restricted
    -v --version            Print the current version
    -d --debug              Run in debug mode with logging (see --logs flag below). Use the LOG_LEVEL env var to set the log level (debug/info/warn/error)
    -l --logs               Tail lazygit logs (intended to be used when `lazygit --debug` is called in a separate terminal tab)
       --profile            Start the profiler and serve it on http port 6060. See CONTRIBUTING.md for more info.
    -c --config             Print the default config
    -cd --print-config-dir   Print the config directory
    -ucd --use-config-dir     override default config directory with provided directory
    -w --work-tree          equivalent of the --work-tree git argument
    -g --git-dir            equivalent of the --git-dir git argument
    -ucf --use-config-file    Comma separated list to custom config file(s)
    -sm --screen-mode        The initial screen-mode, which determines the size of the focused panel. Valid options: 'normal' (default), 'half', 'full'"""

for line in text.splitlines():
    # Find first space after "--"
    idx = line.index("--")
    # Find end of long flag (first space after "--")
    end = line.index(" ", idx)
    long = line[idx:end]
    # Find start of description (first non-space after end)
    j = end
    while j < len(line) and line[j] == " ":
        j += 1
    # prefix (before long): spaces to long start
    prefix = line[:idx]
    # spaces between long end and description
    middle = line[end:j]
    desc = line[j:]
    print(f"prefix={len(prefix)!r} long={long!r}({len(long)}) middle={len(middle)!r} desc_col={j+1}")
EOF

ALL_OK=1
for args in "--help" "-h" "--version" "-v" "-c" "--config" "-cd" "--print-config-dir" "hello" "hello world" "status" "status extra" "--bad" "-bad" "--foo=bar" "-p" "-p /tmp" "-p /tmp/realrepo --version" "-p /tmp/notfound --version" "--help --version" "--version --help" "-c --help" "--help -c" "-d --help" "-ucd /custom --print-config-dir" "-ucd /custom -cd" "--"; do
    ./executable $args > $OUTPUT_DIR/mine_out 2> $OUTPUT_DIR/mine_err
    me_exit=$?
    /tmp/original_keep $args > $OUTPUT_DIR/orig_out 2> $OUTPUT_DIR/orig_err 2>/dev/null || /tmp/original_executable $args > $OUTPUT_DIR/orig_out 2> $OUTPUT_DIR/orig_err
    o_exit=$?
    # strip date stamps
    sed -i 's/^[0-9]\{4\}\/[0-9]\{2\}\/[0-9]\{2\} [0-9:]\{8\}//' $OUTPUT_DIR/mine_err $OUTPUT_DIR/orig_err
    same=1
    diff -q $OUTPUT_DIR/mine_out $OUTPUT_DIR/orig_out >/dev/null || same=0
    diff -q $OUTPUT_DIR/mine_err $OUTPUT_DIR/orig_err >/dev/null || same=0
    [ "$me_exit" == "$o_exit" ] || same=0
    if [ "$same" == "1" ]; then
        echo "OK: [$args]"
    else
        echo "FAIL: [$args] exit_me=$me_exit exit_orig=$o_exit"
        diff $OUTPUT_DIR/mine_out $OUTPUT_DIR/orig_out | head -3
        diff $OUTPUT_DIR/mine_err $OUTPUT_DIR/orig_err | head -3
        ALL_OK=0
    fi
done
echo "======"
[ "$ALL_OK" == "1" ] && echo "ALL OK" || echo "SOME FAILED"

type parseErr struct {

func (e *parseErr) Error() string { return e.msg }

// parseArgs parses command-line arguments similar to flaggy.
// Returns result or a parseErr that will produce help+error output with exit 2.
func parseArgs(argv []string) (*parseResult, error) {
	r := &parseResult{touchedBools: map[string]bool{}}

	i := 0
	for i < len(argv) {
		a := argv[i]
		if a == "" {
			// Treat empty string as positional? For simplicity, treat as positional.
			r.positional = append(r.positional, a)
			i++
			continue
		}
		if strings.HasPrefix(a, "--") {
			// The bare "--" token and everything after it is silently discarded.
			if a == "--" {
				i = len(argv)
				continue
			}
			// long flag
			name := a[2:]
			var value string
			hasValue := false
			if eq := strings.Index(name, "="); eq >= 0 {
				value = name[eq+1:]
				name = name[:eq]
				hasValue = true
			}
			spec := findSpecByLong(name)
			if spec == nil {
				// unknown flag: record as unknown argument.
				if hasValue {
					return nil, &parseErr{msg: "Unknown arguments supplied:  " + name + "=" + value}
				}
				// treat as flag needing value, consume next
				if i+1 >= len(argv) {
					return nil, &parseErr{msg: "Expected a following arg for flag " + name + ", but it did not exist."}
				}
				i += 2
				continue
			}
			if spec.isBool {
				if spec.long != "help" { r.touchedBools[spec.long] = true }
				setBool(r, spec.long, true)
				i++
				continue
			}
			// needs value
			if !hasValue {
				if i+1 >= len(argv) {
					return nil, &parseErr{msg: "Expected a following arg for flag " + name + ", but it did not exist."}
				}
				value = argv[i+1]
				i += 2
			} else {
				i++
			}
			setString(r, spec.long, value)
			continue

All tests pass and the repo is clean. Let me summarize what I did:

**What I reverse-engineered:**
- `lazygit` CLI tool (a terminal UI for git)

**Observed behaviors I reimplemented:**
1. `--version` / `-v`: prints hardcoded version string to stdout
2. `--help` / `-h`: prints auto-generated help text to stderr (with flaggy-style formatting showing `(default: false)` for explicitly-set boolean flags)
3. `--config` / `-c`: prints the embedded default YAML config to stdout
4. `--print-config-dir` / `-cd`: prints resolved config directory path (honouring `-ucd`/`--use-config-dir`, `CONFIG_DIR`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, and `HOME` in correct precedence)
5. `--logs` / `-l`: prints "Tailing log file ..." and tails the log file (or errors if missing)
6. Invalid positional arg (one arg): "Invalid git arg value..." error
7. Too many positionals: help + "Unexpected argument: X"
8. Unknown flag / missing flag value: help + descriptive error, exit 2
9. `-p PATH` validation: "is not a valid git repository" error if path isn't a git repo
10. `--` discards all following arguments (matches flaggy behavior)
11. Default TUI startup error (when we would otherwise enter the TUI) matching the observed stack trace
12. Help output shows program name based on `argv[0]` basename

**What I did not reimplement:**
- The full terminal UI (impractical at ~100k+ LoC)
- Deep config loading, `--use-config-file`, `--work-tree`, `--git-dir` specialised paths

Everything is committed with `.gitignore` excluding build artifacts.
